newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong finance chief delivers handover budget.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong finance chief delivers handover budget.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Donald Tsang has begun delivering his 1997/98 budget speech for the historical year covering the handover of the British colony to China.

The speech, titled "Continuity in a Time of Change" and bound in a gold cover with green lettering, was widely tipped to be a conservative one in light of the monumental political changes confronting the wealthy community of 6.4 million people.
More than 150 years of colonial rule end when Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30, a date now 111 days away.
Tsang consulted China over his budget plans but denied Beijing put any political pressure on Hong Kong fiscal authorities, who have operated independently of Britain for many years.
China has promised Hong Kong autonomy in managing its financial affairs and will permit its capitalist way of life to continue for 50 years after the handover.
Years of windfall surpluses and prudent fiscal management have left Hong Kong awash in cash with reserves of more than HK$300 billion.
Predictions Tsang would reveal a 1996/97 budget surplus far in excess of the HK$1.6 billion he forecast a year earlier have prompted speculation in some quarters of tax cuts.
